author: Mark Atwood
text:
Trait contract reframing — needs explicit owner approval.

The bead reframes enforce_is_draft_atomically from a perf knob (current rustdoc framing) to a correctness-handover contract. If a consumer returns true without actually enforcing, silent data corruption follows.

Note: with the JMAP-h47t.4 fix just landed in 3e33cf8, MemoryBackend now returns true and DOES enforce atomically — so the reference impl is no longer a foot-gun example. The contract issue remains for any consumer-authored backend that overrides this method incorrectly.

Options:
 (a) Stronger rustdoc: rename or relabel as a correctness-handover contract, warn that returning true without enforcing is a spec-violating bug. Cheap, no API break.
 (b) Remove the flag entirely and require ALL backends to enforce isDraft atomically (handler-side pre-fetch path goes away). Workspace-canonical 'backend canonical' rule says this is the right shape. Cost: API break (remove the trait method).
 (c) Invert default: change default to true (assume self-enforcement); backends that want handler-side enforcement must explicitly opt-out. Reduces the foot-gun for consumers who skip the rustdoc.

Recommendation: option (a) for the immediate fix (rustdoc rewrite to call it a contract, not a perf flag). Defer option (b) to a separate workspace-coordinated trait sweep since it touches the handler structure across mail/calendars/tasks. Option (c) is the worst of both — silently changes inherited behavior for downstream consumers.

Escalating because options (b) and (c) are API-shape decisions; (a) alone is do-able as docs but the bead's point is the framing was wrong, not just the wording, so it deserves an owner decision.
